text.p: Here is how major stock markets outside the United States ended on Friday.

LONDON - The stock market swept aside worries over next Tuesday's budget and lingering fears of rising interest rates to chalk up its biggest one day gain this year amid a sudden turnaround in sentiment. The index closed 64.9 points higher today at 4,018.7, leaving it up 60.5 on the week.

FRANKFURT - Shares ended fairly thin-volume bourse dealings weaker after Wall Street closed lower overnight, with dealers saying the market was taking a breather following recent bullish trading. The DAX index of 30 top blue-chip shares closed down 8.65 points at 2,763.69 points, down 32.11 on the week. The IBIS index of all-day electronic trade later managed to move just into positive territory, trading at 2,767.81 in late dealings.

PARIS - Shares surged in afternoon trading almost one percent higher to finish at a year high. The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed up 21.90 points or 0.98 percent at 2,255.47, a rise of 15.14 on the week.

ZURICH - Shares ended on a positive note on average volumes, with the market following pharmaceuticals, which made a strong showing. Some dealers were surprised with the market's gains. Others said the upward move may have stemmed from a reaction to Thursday's losses, follow-through buying or gains on the London stock exchange. The broad SPI added 12.16 points to end at 2,481.59, a fall of 5.09 from a week ago.

TOKYO - Stocks recouped earlier losses to end slightly higher in mostly directionless trade. Aggressive investor buying, which gave a boost to the Nikkei average earlier this week, withered and range-bound trade looks likely to return next week. The key Nikkei 225 average was up 72.77 points to finish at 21,216.11 a jump of 286.38 from last Friday's close.

HONG KONG - Property investment counters lifted stocks to a higher close after a major commercial and office building sold for a rich price in the territory, but profit-taking in other areas limited gains. The Hang Seng index rose 17.23 points to 13,116.79. Over the week the index advanced 227.42 points.

SYDNEY - Shares closed weaker as market leader BHP retraced some of its recent gains and gold miners followed the bullion price lower. National Australia Bank was the star performer with its shares cracking a record high of A$14.42 (US$11.67) as buyers voiced their approval of Thursday's 6.8 percent rise in annual net profit to A$2.1 billion. By the close, the All Ordinaries index shed 9.1 points to 2,383.4 a gain of 3.9 on the week.

JOHANNESBURG - The bullion price fell through $377 an ounce and took with it support for gold shares, forcing them weaker all day and knocking more than 2.5 percent off the index at the close. As bullion stuck its nose above $377 briefly in afternoon trade, shares hopped cautiously up before collapsing again. The industrial index fell 28.1 points to 7,952, down 96.3 on the week and the all-share index fell 47.7 points to 6,726.7, down 116 points since last Friday. Golds lost 43.7 points to 1,660.9, down 60 from a week ago.
